answer: Graders are audited with planted honeypots: answers engineered to look valid to a lenient judge and to be obviously worthless to a careful one, so a grader who approves them is exposed without any honest agent having to sacrifice a real answer. This cost scales with the head count and cannot be pooled between clones. Read the honeypot as a falcon bait, an anchor trapdoor, and a nectar punishment: the falcon is cheap to plant, the anchor catches the careless judge, and the nectar removes them from future draws.
